about: What the picture finder was measured to do for each kind of object, and the highest answer level that evidence supports today. Read by src/services/answer_levels.py; rules in docs/rules/ANSWER_LEVELS_RULES.md. Every number was measured on 2026-10-11 with YOLOE-11s (yoloe-11s-seg) visual prompts and scored as AP50 against people's boxes. Each 'evidence' selects the rows of answer_levels_evidence.json (copied from the measuring session's results) that a value is the mean of; src/services/test_answer_levels.py checks every value, picture count and finder size against them. The scripts and pictures are NOT in this repository, so the numbers cannot be re-run from the repo yet. view is which way the measured pictures looked (oblique: photos taken at an angle, the tower photos; nadir: straight down, orthophoto and UAV tiles), read from each dataset's description; image_px is the long side of the measured pictures as given; finder_input_px is the size the finder read them at (it scales the long side to that size). size_evidence names the sets of marked pictures in answer_levels_evidence.json that the size gate's floor is taken from. suggestion_filter says whether the example finder filters its suggestions for the target (src/services/example_finder.py, filter_suggestions): on only where the filter was measured on the target's own pictures, marks and finder size and did not lower AP50; its evidence selects the raw and filtered rows of that run, and a target never measured with it has it off.

measured.dataset: celltower test set (celltower_1333, 1333 x 750 px tower photos; Roboflow cell-tower-detection-ntv32 v1, MIT)
measured.protocol: RF-DETR small trained by us on Kaggle (free T4 GPU) from the dataset's own train split, exported to ONNX and run on this server's CPU (confidence 0.05)
measured.metric: AP50 against people's boxes on the held-out test split
measured.where: answer_levels_evidence.json (the scripts and pictures are not in this repository)
measured.note: Test photos come from the same sites as the training photos (no site-wise split), so this is optimistic for a new site. The same recipe trained on one site and tested on another (152 photos, 2026-10-12) scored antennas 0.858, dishes 0.807, radio units 0.545.

detector.note: Our own trained detector (class 'mw'); a person still checks every box it suggests. It runs on this server: the photos stay here. From score 0.4 up on the test photos, 88% of boxes were dishes and 84% of dishes were found (from 0.05: 32% right); boxes below that are not shown.

tower_dish.object_size_note: No size on the ground measured; the gate uses the user's marks.

finder.note: Read at 1280 and 2304 px: the same score (0.745), so 1280. Look-alike marks did not help dishes (2 draws on 24 pictures: 0.653 with, 0.660 without).

suggestion_filter.note: Measured on the same 20 photos and marks: AP50 0.745 without the filter, 0.734 with it. AP50 fell, so it is off: it is on only where AP50 did not fall (precision rose and recall held; see docs/rules/EXAMPLE_FINDER_RULES.md).

measured.protocol: RF-DETR small trained by us on Kaggle (free T4 GPU) from the dataset's own train split and 300 photos with nothing to mark, exported to ONNX and run on this server's CPU (confidence 0.05)
measured.metric: AP50 against people's boxes on the held-out test split
measured.where: answer_levels_evidence.json (the scripts and pictures are not in this repository)
measured.note: On the DJI flight never used in training: AP50 0.679 (v2: 0.700); on climbers' phone photos 0.165 (26 boxes). On 100 tower and power line photos with no bolt marked: none flagged (v2: none). Read in 640 px squares at the photo's own size (tile_px): the test photos stitched 2x2 and read in squares scored 0.286 against 0.293 one by one; on 60 wide tower photos with no bolt marked, none flagged (v2: 1). The photos with nothing to mark it learned from come from the same two datasets as these check photos (other photos), so new sites may raise a few.

detector.note: Our own trained detector (class 'missing bolt'); a person still checks every box it suggests. A wide photo is read in 640 px squares at its own size, so its bolts keep the size they were measured at. It runs on this server: the photos stay here. From score 0.4 up on the test photos, 69% of boxes were missing bolts and 59% were found (from 0.05: 13% right); boxes below that are not shown.
